ideas.risks: The needed query may be impossible without already knowing a correlated predictor; the RCN agreement-filter calculation is a serious warning sign.
ideas.summary: Try to prove or refute an observable residual-forcing lemma: if a current randomized predictor still has excess at least epsilon over some near-optimal comparator c, construct a samplable query distribution Q from observable samples and the current predictor such that c has error below gamma on Q. Test loss-gradient, rejection-sampling, and label-randomization constructions against the RCN threshold from iteration 2.
ideas.title: Observable Residual Forcing
ideas.why_promising: This would bypass hidden clean-set enumeration and give a direct boosting route from fixed-slack weak calls to strong agnostic learning.

ideas.risks: Point-mass, empirical-support, and artificial-relabeling queries can break overly broad statements; the theorem must state smoothness and public-information restrictions precisely.
ideas.summary: Generalize the agreement-filter obstruction. In the RCN model Y=f(X)N, characterize public filters or query distributions built from X, Y, and previous public hypotheses. Prove that any polynomial-mass query with conditional noise below gamma must already encode nontrivial correlation or mutual information about f.
ideas.title: Public-Filter Barrier
ideas.why_promising: It turns the solver's local obstruction into a sharper restricted black-box barrier that explorer agents can criticize line by line.

ideas.risks: The audit may show the exponential transcript or clean-label enumeration is essential for the known proof, not an artifact.
ideas.summary: Audit the da Cunha-style residual-free booster at the algorithm level and isolate the exact step causing non-polynomial dependence. For each exponential term, ask whether validation, direct weak calls, online selection, or a capacity assumption on Range(A) can replace enumeration.
ideas.title: De-Enumerate Residual-Free Boosting
ideas.why_promising: This is the closest known positive route: the fixed-slack source matches the semantic weak condition, and only representation-uniform efficiency is missing.

ideas.risks: The atlas source gives an arbitrary learner A, so stability, compression, or small range may be extra assumptions rather than consequences.
ideas.summary: Prove a clean conditional theorem: fixed-slack weak learning plus a polynomial clean-witness menu property, stable transcript property, or small metric entropy for weak outputs implies strong agnostic improper learning. Include exact validation independence and near-1/2 OPT handling.
ideas.title: Structured Weak Learner Theorem
ideas.why_promising: Even if the main edge remains open, this would identify natural additional hypotheses under which the implication is true.

ideas.risks: Most natural candidates fail because low-noise distribution-free weak learning is already hard, or because public structure makes strong improper learning possible.
ideas.summary: Search for a represented class with efficient fixed-slack weak learning below noise gamma but hard recovery under random classification noise eta > gamma. Focus on code-like classes where low-radius weighted unique decoding is efficient while moderate-noise approximate decoding or list recovery is conjecturally hard.
ideas.title: Unique-Decoding Separation Template
ideas.why_promising: The RCN identity gives a crisp route from strong agnostic learning to hidden-comparator recovery, so a suitable class would yield a serious conditional separation.

ideas.risks: A fixed-slack oracle may legally return only the anchor/public hypothesis and ignore the target component; this may become a no-go result.
ideas.summary: Investigate anchor doping: mix the hard target distribution with an easy known realizable distribution to drive OPT below gamma, then quantify whether any valid weak answer must carry target signal. If not, prove a formal anchor-doping obstruction.
ideas.title: Anchor Doping
ideas.why_promising: It tests a natural amplification trick that could force useful weak behavior without identifying clean examples.

ideas.risks: Small finite games may reflect artifacts of tiny domains rather than asymptotic representation-uniform learning.
ideas.summary: Build exact finite-domain minimax models with small X and C. Let the weak oracle choose any response satisfying err <= OPT + beta, and search over bounded adaptive wrappers for either a forced OPT + epsilon learner or a hard adversarial oracle strategy.
ideas.title: Finite Minimax Testbed
ideas.why_promising: Exact small instances can reveal whether the obstruction is geometric, oracle-theoretic, or tied to computational representation issues.
